diagram_classification: geometrical / abstract (possibly cosmological or elemental); the classification is uncertain because the diagram has no labels
interpretation: The diagram is a circular figure made of three colours (grey-blue, red-orange and yellow). Its outer ring is divided into coloured segments. Inside it, arcs of the same three colours cross one another and form a symmetrical interlace around an empty central space. Short blue bars sit at the top, bottom, left and right of the centre. The colours alternate and repeat, and the arcs link the outer circle to the inner field, so the figure looks like a scheme of interrelated parts of one whole. This could stand for the cosmos, the elements or qualities, or the cycle of time. However, no inscription inside the figure names its parts, so any reading of the colours or arcs is tentative. The words at the lower left margin are only partly legible and cannot be used as evidence. The specific meaning of each colour and arc is uninterpreted.
evidence: The figure is circular and has a clear four-fold symmetry (top, bottom, left, right). Three colours are used consistently: blue-grey, red and yellow. The outer ring is segmented by colour. Arcs of the three colours cross and interlace. The central space is empty. Four small blue bars lie near the centre. There are no labels, numbers or names inside the figure. The marginal text at the lower left is fragmentary and cannot be read with confidence.
